cards.developerNotes: Entry-level side-business amount. Flag business-income audit consideration separately.

cards.name: Freelance Net Income — $25,000
cards.description: Your freelance work produced $25,000 of net business income this round.
cards.taxRule: Add $25,000 as net business income. Withholding/prepayments are determined separately.
cards.pathwayRule: Entrepreneur pathway may have additional income draws.
cards.educationMessage: People who work for themselves may need to plan for taxes differently because taxes may not automatically come out of each payment.
cards.resultMessage: $25,000 of net business income has been added for this round.
cards.developerNotes: Business tier 2. Don't automatically set withholding to zero.

cards.name: Small Business Net Income — $35,000
cards.description: Your business produced $35,000 of net income this round.

cards.resultMessage: $35,000 of net business income has been added for this round.

cards.name: Small Business Net Income — $50,000
cards.description: Your business produced $50,000 of net income this round.
cards.taxRule: Add $50,000 as net business income.
cards.pathwayRule: Entrepreneur pathway may have additional income draws.
cards.educationMessage: The simulation uses net business income—the amount remaining after applicable business expenses—not total sales.
cards.resultMessage: $50,000 of net business income has been added for this round.
cards.developerNotes: Middle business tier.

cards.name: Small Business Net Income — $65,000
cards.description: Your business produced $65,000 of net income this round.
cards.taxRule: Add $65,000 as net business income.
cards.pathwayRule: Entrepreneur pathway may have additional income draws.
cards.educationMessage: Self-employed taxpayers generally have additional tax responsibilities that employees may not have.
cards.resultMessage: $65,000 of net business income has been added for this round.
cards.developerNotes: Can support later self-employment-tax lesson.

cards.name: Small Business Net Income — $80,000
cards.description: Your business produced $80,000 of net income this round.
cards.taxRule: Add $80,000 as net business income.
cards.pathwayRule: Entrepreneur pathway may have additional income draws.
cards.educationMessage: Business owners may need to make tax payments during the year instead of relying on employer withholding.
cards.resultMessage: $80,000 of net business income has been added for this round.
cards.developerNotes: Withholding/prepayment deck still determines simulated tax paid in advance.

cards.name: Small Business Net Income — $100,000
cards.description: Your business produced $100,000 of net income this round.
cards.taxRule: Add $100,000 as net business income.
cards.pathwayRule: Entrepreneur pathway may have additional income draws.
cards.educationMessage: As business income grows, planning for taxes and keeping good records becomes increasingly important.
cards.resultMessage: $100,000 of net business income has been added for this round.
cards.developerNotes: Higher business tier.

cards.name: Small Business Net Income — $125,000
cards.description: Your business produced $125,000 of net income this round.
cards.taxRule: Add $125,000 as net business income.
cards.pathwayRule: Entrepreneur pathway may have additional income draws.
cards.educationMessage: Higher business income can mean a larger tax obligation and makes tax planning especially important.
cards.resultMessage: $125,000 of net business income has been added for this round.
cards.developerNotes: Highest regular business tier in initial deck.

cards.name: Social Security — $18,000
cards.description: Social Security is your only retirement income this round.
cards.taxRule: $18,000 SSA income; no additional retirement/investment income. Apply Social Security taxation rules in tax engine.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Social Security can provide retirement income, but relying on it alone may mean living on a limited income.
cards.resultMessage: You received $18,000 from Social Security and had no other retirement income this round.
cards.developerNotes: Lower SSA-only outcome. Do not assume all Social Security is taxable.

cards.name: Social Security — $24,000
cards.description: Social Security is your only retirement income this round.
cards.taxRule: $24,000 SSA income; no additional retirement/investment income. Apply Social Security taxation rules in tax engine.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Social Security provides a base of retirement income. Whether some benefits are taxable can depend on your other income.
cards.resultMessage: You received $24,000 from Social Security and had no other retirement income this round.
cards.developerNotes: Middle SSA-only outcome.

cards.name: Social Security — $32,000
cards.description: You delayed benefits and now receive a larger Social Security benefit, with no additional retirement income this round.
cards.taxRule: $32,000 SSA income; no additional retirement/investment income. Apply Social Security taxation rules in tax engine.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: When you begin Social Security can affect the size of your monthly benefit. Waiting longer can result in a larger benefit, up to applicable limits.
cards.resultMessage: You receive $32,000 in Social Security income this round.
cards.developerNotes: Represents comparatively higher SSA benefit; educational simplification rather than individualized benefit calculation.

cards.name: Social Security + Small Retirement Fund
cards.description: You receive $22,000 from Social Security plus $8,000 from retirement savings.
cards.taxRule: Components: $22,000 SSA + $8,000 retirement distribution. Calculate each component under applicable rules.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Retirement income can come from more than one place. Savings can supplement the income you receive from Social Security.
cards.resultMessage: Your retirement income totals $30,000: $22,000 from Social Security and $8,000 from retirement savings.
cards.developerNotes: Lowest mixed-retirement outcome. Engine should retain components separately.

cards.name: Social Security + Retirement Savings
cards.description: You receive $24,000 from Social Security plus $16,000 from retirement savings.
cards.taxRule: Components: $24,000 SSA + $16,000 retirement distribution. Calculate components separately.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Saving during your working years can create another source of money alongside Social Security in retirement.
cards.resultMessage: Your retirement income totals $40,000 from Social Security and retirement savings.
cards.developerNotes: Lower-middle mixed outcome.

cards.name: Social Security + Strong Retirement Savings
cards.description: You receive $28,000 from Social Security plus $32,000 from retirement savings and investments.
cards.taxRule: Components: $28,000 SSA + $32,000 retirement/investment income. Calculate components separately.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Building retirement savings during your career can give you more than one source of income later in life.
cards.resultMessage: Your combined retirement income is $60,000 this round.
cards.developerNotes: Comfortable mixed outcome.

incomeComponents.sourceDescription: Workbook does not separate the $32,000 retirement/investment component.

cards.name: Social Security + Large Retirement Portfolio
cards.description: You receive $30,000 from Social Security plus $55,000 from retirement accounts and investments.

cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Having more retirement income can improve financial security, but different types of retirement income can also have different tax consequences.
cards.resultMessage: Your combined retirement income is $85,000 this round.
cards.developerNotes: Upper mixed outcome. Good introduction to retirement-income tax differences.

incomeComponents.sourceDescription: Workbook does not separate the $55,000 retirement/investment component.

cards.name: Social Security + Successful Investment Portfolio
cards.description: You receive $32,000 from Social Security plus $88,000 from retirement accounts and investments.
cards.taxRule: Components: $32,000 SSA + $88,000 retirement/investment income. Tax treatment depends on source.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Retirement does not necessarily mean low income. Investments and retirement accounts can create substantial income after you stop working.
cards.resultMessage: Your retirement income totals $120,000 this round. Your income sources may receive different tax treatment.
cards.developerNotes: First high-asset outcome.

incomeComponents.sourceDescription: Workbook does not separate the $88,000 retirement/investment component.

cards.name: Social Security + High-Value Portfolio
cards.description: You receive $36,000 from Social Security plus $164,000 from retirement accounts and investments.
cards.taxRule: Components: $36,000 SSA + $164,000 retirement/investment income. Tax treatment depends on source.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: A high-income retiree can still have a significant tax bill. Retirement does not automatically mean your income becomes tax-free.
cards.resultMessage: Your combined retirement income is $200,000 this round. The tax engine will consider the different income sources.
cards.developerNotes: Intentionally large outcome to challenge assumption that retirees always have low taxable income.

incomeComponents.sourceDescription: Workbook does not separate the $164,000 retirement/investment component.

cards.name: Investment-Funded Retirement — $300,000
cards.description: Your investment portfolio produces $300,000 of retirement income. Social Security is not included in this scenario.
cards.taxRule: $300,000 investment/retirement income; no SSA component on this card. Actual tax treatment will depend on modeled investment types.
cards.pathwayRule: Early Retiree accesses retirement deck beginning Round 4.
cards.educationMessage: Some retirees receive much more income from investments and retirement assets than from Social Security. High retirement income can still create substantial taxes.
cards.resultMessage: Your investments produce $300,000 of retirement income this round, with no Social Security included in this scenario.
cards.developerNotes: Extreme high-asset card. Later decide whether income represents taxable distributions, gains, dividends, or simplified blended investment income.

incomeComponents.normalizationNote: Canonicalized the combined-income label; the workbook does not identify the source mix or tax treatment.

cards.name: Had a Child
cards.description: You welcomed a new child into your household.
cards.taxRule: Add 1 dependent. If income qualifies, receive the Child Tax Credit of $X for the current tax year.
cards.pathwayRule: Caregiver's permanent dependent is separate and remains active.
cards.educationMessage: Having a qualifying child can change your taxes and may make you eligible for the Child Tax Credit.
cards.resultMessage: Your household grew by one dependent. The app will check your income and current-year rules to determine your Child Tax Credit of $X.
cards.developerNotes: $X is retrieved from Tax Rules for selected Tax Year. Do not hard-code credit amount on physical card. Game treats child as qualifying for the simplified child-credit scenario while active.

cards.name: Became a Caregiver
cards.description: You began financially supporting a qualifying family member.
cards.taxRule: Add 1 dependent. If income qualifies, receive the Other Dependent Credit of $X for the current tax year.
cards.pathwayRule: Caregiver Pathway still maintains its separate permanent dependent.
cards.educationMessage: Supporting a qualifying dependent may make you eligible for a dependent-related tax credit.
cards.resultMessage: You added a qualifying dependent. The app will check your income and current-year rules to determine your Other Dependent Credit of $X.
cards.developerNotes: $X retrieved from Tax Rules. Life Event dependent is tracked separately from Caregiver Pathway dependent.

cards.name: Got Married
cards.description: You got married and your household filing situation changed.
cards.taxRule: Change filing status to Married Filing Jointly. Add one spouse earned-income source matching the applicable primary Income card, then use the current-year married deduction and federal tax brackets. Do not double additional income, investments, retirement income, credits or deductions.
cards.pathwayRule: No special Pathway rule.
cards.educationMessage: Marriage can change the filing status, standard deduction, and tax brackets used on your return.
cards.resultMessage: Your filing status is now Married Filing Jointly. The app will apply the current-year married tax rules.
cards.developerNotes: If already married, redraw. Filing status remains MFJ until another Life Event changes it. Current-year values come from Tax Rules.

cards.name: Got Divorced
cards.description: Your marriage ended and your filing situation changed.
cards.taxRule: Remove married status and spouse earned income. Use Head of Household when an active qualifying household dependent remains; otherwise use Single. Existing dependents remain unless separately removed or expired.
cards.pathwayRule: No special Pathway rule.
cards.educationMessage: Divorce can change the filing status and tax rules used on your return.
cards.resultMessage: You are now unmarried. The app will use Head of Household if an active qualifying dependent remains, or Single otherwise, and remove spouse earned income.
cards.developerNotes: If player is not currently married, redraw. Do not automatically remove dependents. TASK 10.15.05 derives HOH or Single from the current unmarried household and removes spouse earned income.

cards.name: Bought a Home
cards.description: You purchased a home and became a homeowner.
cards.taxRule: Activate Homeowner status. You are now eligible for applicable homeowner-related deduction scenarios. The app still compares allowable itemized deductions with standard deduction X.
cards.pathwayRule: Home Builder begins with Homeowner status already active; if already homeowner, redraw.
cards.educationMessage: Owning a home may create expenses considered when itemizing, but homeownership does not automatically make itemizing better.
cards.resultMessage: You are now a homeowner. Homeowner-related deduction scenarios are available, but the app will still compare your itemized deductions with standard deduction X.
cards.developerNotes: Does not create a fixed deduction. Homeowner status enables applicable scenarios. Do not automatically force itemization.

cards.name: Dependent Left Household
cards.description: A dependent you were supporting is no longer part of your qualifying household.
cards.taxRule: Remove 1 applicable dependent. Remove the associated dependent credit when that dependent is no longer eligible.
cards.pathwayRule: Caregiver Pathway cannot lose its permanent pathway-dependent.
cards.educationMessage: When someone is no longer your qualifying dependent, the tax benefits associated with that dependent can also change.
cards.resultMessage: You have one fewer qualifying dependent. The app will recalculate any dependent-related credit affected by the change.
cards.developerNotes: If player has no removable dependent, redraw. Never reduce Caregiver below pathway minimum of 1 dependent.

cards.name: Spouse Joined Household
cards.description: You got married and now file as a married household in the game.
cards.taxRule: Change filing status to Married Filing Jointly. Add one spouse earned-income source matching the applicable primary Income card, then use the current-year married deduction and federal tax brackets. Do not double additional income, investments, retirement income, credits or deductions.
cards.pathwayRule: No special Pathway rule.
cards.educationMessage: Getting married can change the filing status, deductions, and tax brackets used to calculate federal income tax.
cards.resultMessage: Your filing status is now Married Filing Jointly. The app will apply the current-year married tax rules.
cards.developerNotes: Second marriage Life Event for deck variety. If already married, redraw. Current-year amounts and brackets come from Tax Rules.

cards.name: Parent Moved In
cards.description: A parent moved into your household and now qualifies as your dependent in the game.
cards.taxRule: Add 1 Other Dependent. If income qualifies, receive the Other Dependent Credit of $X for the current tax year.
cards.pathwayRule: Caregiver Pathway's permanent dependent remains separate.
cards.educationMessage: Supporting a qualifying parent may make you eligible for the Other Dependent Credit.
cards.resultMessage: Your parent qualifies as an Other Dependent in the game. The app will check your income and current-year rules to determine your credit of $X.
cards.developerNotes: Game assumes qualifying-relative requirements are satisfied while card is active. $X retrieved from current Tax Rules.

cards.name: Sold Home and Began Renting
cards.description: You sold your home and moved into a rental.
cards.taxRule: Remove Homeowner status. Homeowner-only deduction scenarios are no longer available.
cards.pathwayRule: Home Builder loses Homeowner status if this event occurs despite beginning game as homeowner.
cards.educationMessage: Selling a home can change which expenses are available when comparing itemized deductions with the standard deduction.
cards.resultMessage: You are now renting. Homeowner-only deduction scenarios are no longer available.
cards.developerNotes: If player is not currently a homeowner, redraw. Do not model home-sale capital gain in initial curriculum.

cards.name: Added a Second Dependent
cards.description: Another qualifying dependent joined your household.
cards.taxRule: Add 1 dependent. If income and dependent type qualify, receive the applicable dependent credit of $X for the current tax year.
cards.pathwayRule: Caregiver permanent dependent counts separately; this card may add another dependent above pathway minimum.
cards.educationMessage: Adding another qualifying dependent may change the tax credits available on your return.
cards.resultMessage: You added another qualifying dependent. The app will determine which dependent credit applies and display the current-year amount of $X.
cards.developerNotes: App must identify applicable simplified dependent type so it can retrieve the correct $X. Do not hard-code credit amount on physical card.

cards.name: Medical Expenses — $3,000
cards.description: You had $3,000 of qualifying medical expenses, but your combined eligible itemized deductions remained below your standard deduction of X.
cards.taxRule: Compare eligible itemized deductions to current standard deduction X. Scenario is designed so itemized total remains below X; use standard deduction when X is larger.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Having a deductible expense does not automatically mean itemizing is better. You compare your eligible itemized deductions with the standard deduction.
cards.resultMessage: Your eligible itemized deductions did not exceed X. The standard deduction gives you the larger deduction this round.
cards.developerNotes: X comes from tax-rules table based on applicable year and filing status. Medical limitations handled by engine.

cards.name: Charitable Giving — $2,500
cards.description: You gave $2,500 to qualifying charities, but your combined eligible itemized deductions remained below X.
cards.taxRule: Add eligible charitable giving to itemized deductions and compare the combined total with X. Use standard deduction when X is larger.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: A charitable contribution may count toward itemized deductions, but itemizing only helps when the eligible total beats the standard deduction.
cards.resultMessage: Your itemized total stayed below X, so the standard deduction is better this round.
cards.developerNotes: Assume qualifying and documented charitable contribution for game purposes.

cards.name: Mortgage Interest — $6,000
cards.description: You paid $6,000 of qualifying mortgage interest, but your total eligible itemized deductions still did not exceed X.
cards.taxRule: Include eligible mortgage interest in itemized total. Compare combined itemized deductions with X.
cards.pathwayRule: Requires active homeowner status or redraw.
cards.educationMessage: Owning a home does not automatically make itemizing better. Mortgage interest is one part of the itemized-deduction comparison.
cards.resultMessage: Even with your mortgage interest, your itemized deductions stayed below X. The standard deduction is larger.
cards.developerNotes: Requires active homeowner Life Event.

cards.name: Several Small Deductions — $8,500
cards.description: You had several eligible itemized expenses totaling $8,500, but together they were still below X.
cards.taxRule: Eligible itemized total is $8,500. Compare against current X and use the larger allowable deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Itemized deductions are added together and compared with the standard deduction. Several deductions can still be too small to make itemizing worthwhile.
cards.resultMessage: Your eligible itemized expenses totaled $8,500, but X was larger. You take the standard deduction.
cards.developerNotes: General mixed-expense scenario.

cards.name: Medical + Charitable Expenses — $9,500
cards.description: You had qualifying medical and charitable expenses, but your combined eligible itemized deductions totaled only $9,500.
cards.taxRule: Eligible itemized total is $9,500. Compare against X and use the larger allowable deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Even when you have more than one type of deductible expense, the standard deduction may still be larger.
cards.resultMessage: Your itemized deductions totaled $9,500. Because that was below X, the standard deduction gives you the better result.
cards.developerNotes: Highest planned below-X scenario.

cards.name: Major Medical Expenses ? $8,000 Above X
cards.description: Major medical expenses, together with other eligible itemized expenses, made your total allowable itemized deductions $8,000 more than X.
cards.taxRule: Total allowable itemized deductions = X + $8,000. Compare with X and use the larger deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: Homeowner status may contribute mortgage-interest component when applicable.
cards.educationMessage: Medical expenses are one example of qualifying itemized expenses. In this game, your combined allowable itemized deductions are X plus $8,000. The medical expenses are not an extra amount to deduct.
cards.resultMessage: Your combined allowable itemized deductions were $8,000 more than X, so itemizing gives you the larger deduction.
cards.graphic: Medical bills + mortgage + donations crossing threshold
cards.developerNotes: Simplified game rule (approved): total allowable itemized deductions = standard deduction + $8,000. Medical expenses are an example only; do not deduct them again.

cards.name: Mortgage Interest ? $9,000 Above X
cards.description: Mortgage interest, together with other eligible itemized expenses, made your total allowable itemized deductions $9,000 more than X.
cards.taxRule: Total allowable itemized deductions = X + $9,000. Compare with X and use the larger deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: Requires active homeowner status or redraw.
cards.educationMessage: Mortgage interest is one example of qualifying itemized expenses for homeowners. In this game, your combined allowable itemized deductions are X plus $9,000. The mortgage interest is not an extra amount to deduct.
cards.resultMessage: Your combined allowable itemized deductions were $9,000 more than X, so itemizing gives you the larger deduction this round.
cards.developerNotes: Simplified game rule (approved): total allowable itemized deductions = standard deduction + $9,000. Requires homeowner Life Event. Mortgage interest is an example only; do not deduct it again.

cards.name: Charitable Giving ? $10,000 Above X
cards.description: Charitable contributions, together with other eligible itemized expenses, made your total allowable itemized deductions $10,000 more than X.
cards.taxRule: Total allowable itemized deductions = X + $10,000. Compare with X and use the larger deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Charitable giving is one example of qualifying itemized expenses. In this game, your combined allowable itemized deductions are X plus $10,000. The contributions are not an extra amount to deduct.
cards.resultMessage: Your combined allowable itemized deductions were $10,000 more than X, so itemizing gives you the larger deduction.
cards.developerNotes: Simplified game rule (approved): total allowable itemized deductions = standard deduction + $10,000. Assume qualifying/documented contribution; it is an example only and is not deducted again.

cards.name: High-Deduction Year — $18,000
cards.description: Several major deductible expenses occurred during the same period. Your total allowable itemized deductions for this round are $18,000.
cards.taxRule: Total allowable itemized deductions = $18,000. Compare with current X and use whichever deduction is larger.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Your best deduction method can change from year to year. A year with unusually high eligible expenses may make itemizing more valuable.
cards.resultMessage: This was a high-deduction year. The app compared your itemized deductions with X and selected the larger allowable deduction.
cards.developerNotes: Simplified game rule (approved): $18,000 is the total allowable itemized deductions for the round. Do not automatically force itemization. Future X could exceed $18,000 depending on tax year/status.

cards.name: Major Itemized Expenses — $25,000
cards.description: Mortgage interest, charitable contributions, medical expenses, and other eligible items created $25,000 of itemized expenses this round.
cards.taxRule: Calculate allowable itemized deductions and compare with current X. Use the larger allowable deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: Homeownership may modify narrative/components if active.
cards.educationMessage: The standard deduction and allowable itemized deductions are compared. The simulation uses the option that produces the larger allowable deduction.
cards.resultMessage: Your eligible itemized deductions were compared with X. The larger allowable deduction will be used to calculate your taxable income.
cards.developerNotes: High-deduction scenario. Tax engine remains source of truth rather than card's Above X label.

cards.name: Very Little Paid in Advance — 40%
cards.description: Only about 40% of your calculated tax was paid during the year.
cards.taxRule: After calculating tax, treat 40% of calculated tax as already paid. Compare total tax with tax prepaid to determine refund or amount due.
cards.pathwayRule: Corporate Climber may redraw once if prepayment is below 90%.
cards.educationMessage: Taxes are often paid throughout the year. Employees may have taxes withheld from paychecks, while self-employed people may make estimated tax payments.
cards.resultMessage: You prepaid about 40% of your calculated tax. A significant amount remains due when you file.
cards.developerNotes: Strong underpayment scenario. Do not treat remaining balance as additional tax.

cards.name: Not Enough Paid in Advance — 60%
cards.description: About 60% of your calculated tax was paid during the year.
cards.taxRule: Treat 60% of calculated tax as already paid. Compare total tax with tax prepaid.
cards.pathwayRule: Corporate Climber may redraw once if prepayment is below 90%.
cards.educationMessage: Paying some tax during the year does not guarantee that enough was paid to cover your final tax bill.
cards.resultMessage: You prepaid about 60% of your calculated tax. You still have an amount due when you file.
cards.developerNotes: Works with W-2 or business income. Penalties are handled separately.

cards.name: Came Up Short — 80%
cards.description: You paid most of your calculated tax during the year, but your payments still came up short.
cards.taxRule: Treat 80% of calculated tax as already paid. Compare total tax with tax prepaid.
cards.pathwayRule: Corporate Climber may redraw once if prepayment is below 90%.
cards.educationMessage: You can pay taxes throughout the year and still owe something when you file if your payments were less than your final calculated tax.
cards.resultMessage: You prepaid about 80% of your calculated tax. You'll need to pay the remaining difference when you file.
cards.developerNotes: Mild underpayment. Does not automatically trigger an underpayment penalty.

cards.name: Almost Covered — 90%
cards.description: Your tax payments were close to your final calculated tax, but you paid slightly less during the year.
cards.taxRule: Treat 90% of calculated tax as already paid. Compare total tax with tax prepaid.
cards.pathwayRule: No redraw benefit; 90% meets Corporate Climber redraw threshold.
cards.educationMessage: Owing a small amount when you file does not necessarily mean your taxes were higher. It may simply mean you paid slightly less during the year.
cards.resultMessage: You prepaid about 90% of your calculated tax. You'll settle the remaining difference when you file.
cards.developerNotes: Near-target scenario. Keep separate from actual penalty rules.

cards.name: Right on Target — 100%
cards.description: Your payments during the year closely matched your final calculated tax.
cards.taxRule: Treat 100% of calculated tax as already paid. Filing result should be approximately $0 before other applicable effects.
cards.pathwayRule: No special pathway action needed.
cards.educationMessage: Paying close to the amount ultimately owed can mean neither a large refund nor a large balance due.
cards.resultMessage: Your tax payments closely matched your calculated tax. You're approximately even when you file.
cards.developerNotes: Neutral outcome. Do not present a $0 refund as losing.

cards.name: A Little Extra Paid — 105%
cards.description: You paid slightly more during the year than your final calculated tax.
cards.taxRule: Treat 105% of calculated tax as already paid. Excess tax prepaid becomes simulated refund.
cards.pathwayRule: No special pathway action needed.
cards.educationMessage: A refund generally means you paid more toward your taxes during the year than your final tax calculation required.
cards.resultMessage: You prepaid about 105% of your calculated tax. The extra amount comes back to you as a refund.
cards.developerNotes: Small-refund scenario.

cards.name: Extra Paid Throughout the Year — 115%
cards.description: Your payments during the year exceeded your final calculated tax.
cards.taxRule: Treat 115% of calculated tax as already paid. Excess tax prepaid becomes simulated refund.
cards.pathwayRule: No special pathway action needed.
cards.educationMessage: A tax refund is generally money you already paid that exceeded your final tax obligation. It is not automatically bonus money.
cards.resultMessage: You prepaid about 115% of your calculated tax. The excess becomes your refund.
cards.developerNotes: Important misconception-busting card.

cards.name: Much More Paid Than Needed — 130%
cards.description: You paid considerably more during the year than your final calculated tax required.
cards.taxRule: Treat 130% of calculated tax as already paid. Excess tax prepaid becomes simulated refund.
cards.pathwayRule: No special pathway action needed.
cards.educationMessage: A larger refund can feel good, but it may also mean you had less of your own money available during the year.
cards.resultMessage: You prepaid about 130% of your calculated tax. You'll receive the excess back as a larger refund.
cards.developerNotes: Do not describe large refund as automatically good or bad. Focus on cash-flow tradeoff.

cards.name: You Adjusted Mid-Year — 100%
cards.description: You noticed your tax payments were off track and changed them during the year.
cards.taxRule: Treat final tax prepayments as approximately 100% of calculated tax after a mid-year adjustment.
cards.pathwayRule: No special pathway action needed.
cards.educationMessage: Tax payments can be adjusted when income or life circumstances change. Employees may update withholding, while self-employed people may adjust estimated payments.
cards.resultMessage: You adjusted your tax payments during the year and finished close to your final calculated tax.
cards.developerNotes: Important card because it teaches that prepayment is something taxpayers can actively manage.

cards.name: Nothing Paid in Advance — 0%
cards.description: No federal income tax was paid toward your simulated tax obligation during the year.
cards.taxRule: Treat $0 as tax paid in advance. Calculated tax remains due at filing before other applicable effects.
cards.pathwayRule: Corporate Climber may redraw once because prepayment is below 90%.
cards.educationMessage: If no tax is paid during the year, the tax obligation does not disappear. Employees and business owners are both responsible for making sure enough tax is paid.
cards.resultMessage: You paid nothing toward your calculated tax during the year. Your calculated tax remains due when you file.
cards.developerNotes: Do not label as a 1099-only outcome. Any income pathway can encounter insufficient prepayment in the game. Penalties handled separately.

cards.name: Surprise Work Bonus
cards.description: Great news! Your employer rewards you with an unexpected $7,500 bonus.
cards.taxRule: Add $7,500 to W-2 income for this round. Include it when calculating the player's total income and tax.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: A work bonus is extra income. Even though it wasn't part of your regular salary, it still affects your tax situation.
cards.resultMessage: Nice bonus! $7,500 has been added to your W-2 income for this round.
cards.developerNotes: Add to existing W-2 income rather than replace Income card.

cards.description: You receive a $25,000 inheritance from a family member.
cards.taxRule: Add $25,000 to simulated financial resources, but do not automatically add it to ordinary taxable income.

cards.educationMessage: Receiving money does not always mean it is taxed the same way as wages or business income. The source of money matters.
cards.resultMessage: You received a $25,000 inheritance. Your financial resources increased, but the game does not treat the inheritance itself as ordinary wage income.
cards.developerNotes: Requires financial-resource concept if game tracks cash/wealth. Do not automatically treat inheritance itself as ordinary income.

cards.description: Life happens. You face an unexpected $5,000 expense. Whether it affects your taxes depends on what kind of expense it is.
cards.taxRule: If tied to an eligible business activity, engine may reduce applicable business net income under simplified game rules. If personal, reduce financial resources only and do not automatically create a tax deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: Business-income players may receive business-expense treatment when game conditions qualify.
cards.educationMessage: A big expense is not automatically tax deductible. Business and personal expenses can receive very different tax treatment.
cards.resultMessage: The $5,000 expense has been classified. The app will apply the appropriate business or personal treatment.
cards.graphic: Broken laptop / car repair / surprise bill

cards.resultMessage: You had $4,000 of qualifying education expenses. The app will check the current rules to determine what tax benefit applies.

cards.name: Starter Investment
cards.description: You start investing for the future. Your investment produces a small amount of income over time and grows into a retirement asset.
cards.taxRule: Gain one Starter Investment asset. Add $500 of simulated investment income in each future regular-life round. At retirement, add $10,000 to simulated retirement assets/resources.
cards.pathwayRule: Investor-related pathway rules may modify this asset later if such pathway exists.
cards.educationMessage: Starting small can still matter over time. Investments may produce income while you own them and can become part of your retirement resources.
cards.resultMessage: You acquired a Starter Investment. Keep the investment piece. It adds $500 of investment income in future rounds and $10,000 to your retirement resources.
cards.graphic: Small plant growing from coin / investment token
cards.developerNotes: Amount = retirement addition ($10K). Effect Value = recurring future-round income ($500). Player keeps physical investment token through retirement. Values are game simulation, not promised returns.

cards.name: Everything Checks Out
cards.description: Your return was reviewed. The information was accurate and no changes are needed.
cards.taxRule: End audit with no changes to income, deductions, tax, prepayments, refund, or amount due.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationConcept: Audits Do Not Automatically Mean Errors
cards.educationMessage: Being selected for an audit does not automatically mean something is wrong. A review can end with no changes to the return.
cards.resultMessage: Everything checks out. Your return stays exactly as filed.
cards.developerNotes: Clean audit outcome. Audit ends immediately.

cards.name: Records to the Rescue
cards.description: Your records and receipts support the information being reviewed. No adjustment is required.
cards.taxRule: Treat questioned item as supported. No tax adjustment is made.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Keeping organized records can help you support income, expenses, and deductions reported on a tax return.
cards.resultMessage: Good records paid off. You supported the questioned information and no change is needed.
cards.developerNotes: Especially useful if player has deductions, business income, or investments. Does not create a deduction; it only supports an existing item.

cards.name: Small Error Correction
cards.description: The review finds a small mistake. Correct the affected information and calculate the return again.
cards.taxRule: Select an eligible minor calculation/input error, correct it, and rerun the tax calculation. Correction may increase or decrease the filing result.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Finding an error does not automatically mean a penalty. A correction can increase tax, decrease tax, or sometimes change a refund.
cards.resultMessage: A small error was found and corrected. Your tax result has been recalculated using the corrected information.
cards.developerNotes: Engine should generate/select a small predefined correction. Do not randomly alter arbitrary tax values.

cards.name: Unsupported Deduction
cards.description: Part of an itemized deduction cannot be supported by the required records in this simulation.
cards.taxRule: Remove $2,500 from eligible itemized deductions, then rerun standard-versus-itemized comparison using current X.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Claiming a deduction and being able to support it are two different things. Records can matter when deductions are reviewed.
cards.resultMessage: $2,500 of your itemized deductions could not be supported. Your deduction and tax calculation will be updated.
cards.graphic: Receipt with question mark / subtraction symbol
cards.developerNotes: If player did not itemize or has no applicable deduction, redraw or use context-aware audit result selection.

cards.name: Standard Deduction Now Wins
cards.description: A questioned itemized deduction is removed. Your remaining itemized deductions are now below X.
cards.taxRule: Reduce applicable itemized deduction enough to require a new comparison. If remaining allowable itemized deductions are below X, switch player to standard deduction.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Your deduction choice can change when the facts change. If allowable itemized deductions fall below the standard deduction, the standard deduction may become the better option.
cards.resultMessage: After the audit adjustment, your itemized deductions are below X. The simulation now uses your standard deduction.
cards.graphic: Balance scale tipping from itemized to standard
cards.developerNotes: Only eligible when player originally itemized. Context-aware selection strongly preferred over redraw.

cards.name: Income Was Left Out
cards.description: The review discovers $5,000 of taxable income that was not included in the original calculation.
cards.taxRule: Add $5,000 of taxable income and rerun applicable tax calculations. Do not automatically apply a penalty unless another rule specifically requires one.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Income can come from many sources. Leaving taxable income off a return can change the amount of tax owed.
cards.resultMessage: The review found $5,000 of taxable income that was missing. Your tax calculation has been updated.
cards.developerNotes: Generic omitted-income scenario. Additional tax is calculated by engine rather than hard-coded.

cards.name: Business Expense Questioned
cards.description: A $4,000 expense claimed as a business expense was actually personal or could not be supported.
cards.taxRule: Add $4,000 back to business net income because the expense is disallowed in the simulation. Recalculate tax.
cards.pathwayRule: None
cards.educationMessage: Business expenses need to be legitimate business expenses and properly supported. Personal spending does not become deductible just because someone owns a business.
cards.resultMessage: $4,000 was added back to your business net income. Your tax calculation will be updated.
cards.graphic: Business receipt + personal icon / magnifying glass
cards.developerNotes: Only eligible when player has business/freelance income. Use context-aware audit-result selection.

cards.name: Additional Tax + Penalty
cards.description: The review finds a significant problem that results in additional tax and a simulated penalty.
cards.taxRule: Apply a predefined audit adjustment, recalculate tax, then calculate any game penalty using the current Tax Rules table. Do not hard-code annual penalty rates on this card.
cards.pathwayRule: Pathway rules may modify audit consequences if designed later.
cards.educationMessage: Additional tax and a penalty are not the same thing. Additional tax corrects the tax obligation; a penalty is a separate consequence that may apply under specific rules.
cards.resultMessage: The audit changed your tax calculation and resulted in a penalty. The app will show the additional tax and penalty separately.
cards.graphic: Tax bill split into Tax + Penalty
cards.developerNotes: Higher-severity audit outcome. Exact penalty belongs in Tax Rules so annual rules can be updated without changing physical cards.

pathways.name: Corporate Climber
pathways.shortDescription: You focus on moving up financially throughout your career.
pathways.startingCondition: Draw one Income card in Round 1 and use its dollar amount as your starting primary income.
pathways.advantageRule: Your primary income can never decrease. Each round, draw a new Income card. If its amount is higher than your current primary income, use the new amount. If it is lower, keep your current income amount.
pathways.challengeRule: A lower Income card does not reduce your income, but it also provides no increase that round.
pathways.incomeRule: Draw one Income card each regular-life round. Compare its dollar amount with current primary income and use the higher amount. Ignore W-2/business classification when applying the pathway's climbing rule.
pathways.retirementRule: Normal retirement rules plus accumulated investments.
pathways.educationMessage: Income does not always move in a straight line, but this pathway simulates a career focused on maintaining or increasing earnings over time.
pathways.resultMessage: You kept climbing. Even when new opportunities offered less income, you maintained the highest income level you had reached.
pathways.developerNotes: Store current primary income. Each round use max(currentPrimaryIncome, drawnIncomeAmount). Preserve underlying Income card tax classification for tax calculations even though pathway comparison uses only dollar amount.

pathways.name: Entrepreneur
pathways.shortDescription: You pursue opportunities to earn additional income by building businesses and taking on new ventures.
pathways.startingCondition: Draw one Income card and use its dollar amount as your primary income.
pathways.advantageRule: Once per regular-life round, you may draw one additional Income card and keep it only if it is Business Income.
pathways.challengeRule: Additional business income may introduce business/self-employment tax rules and additional recordkeeping responsibilities.
pathways.incomeRule: Primary income may come from either Income category. Once per regular-life round, player may draw one additional Income card and keep it only if it is Business Income.
pathways.deductionRule: Eligible business expenses may affect net business income when applicable.
pathways.prepaymentRule: Tax Prepayment applies normally. Business income may involve estimated-payment concepts through Tax Rules.
pathways.wildcardRule: Business-related Wildcards apply normally and may stack with other income.
pathways.auditRule: Eligible for business-specific Audit Results when business income is active.
pathways.retirementRule: Normal retirement rules plus accumulated investments.
pathways.educationMessage: Entrepreneurship can create additional opportunities to earn income, while also introducing different tax responsibilities and recordkeeping needs.
pathways.resultMessage: Your willingness to pursue new opportunities gave you additional ways to earn income throughout your tax life.
pathways.developerNotes: Maximum one pathway-generated additional Income draw per regular-life round. Preserve tax classification of all retained Income cards.

pathways.name: Caregiver
pathways.shortDescription: Supporting another person is a lasting part of your financial life.
pathways.startingCondition: Begin the game with 1 permanent pathway-dependent.
pathways.advantageRule: You always have at least one dependent throughout the entire game, including retirement.
pathways.challengeRule: Having a dependent does not automatically make household expenses deductible. Applicable tax benefits still depend on Tax Rules.
pathways.lifeEventRule: Start with one permanent pathway-dependent. Life Events may add or remove other dependents, but they cannot reduce the player's total number of dependents below one.
pathways.deductionRule: Dependent-related tax benefits are evaluated using Tax Rules.
pathways.retirementRule: Your pathway-dependent remains active during retirement. Applicable dependent-related rules continue to be evaluated by the Tax Rules engine.
pathways.educationMessage: Supporting another person can affect a tax return, but having a dependent does not mean every household expense becomes deductible.
pathways.resultMessage: Caring for another person remained part of your financial life from your working years through retirement.
pathways.developerNotes: Set minimumDependents = 1 for entire game. Other dependents can be added or removed normally, but total dependents cannot fall below 1.

pathways.name: Home Builder
pathways.shortDescription: Homeownership becomes an important part of your financial and tax life.
pathways.startingCondition: Begin the game with Homeowner status active.
pathways.advantageRule: You begin the game eligible for homeowner-related deduction scenarios.
pathways.challengeRule: Owning a home does not automatically mean itemizing is better than taking the standard deduction.
pathways.lifeEventRule: If Bought a Home is drawn while already a homeowner, redraw. Sold Home and Began Renting can remove Homeowner status.
pathways.deductionRule: Mortgage/homeowner-related Deduction cards are eligible while Homeowner status is active. The engine still compares allowable itemized deductions against X.
pathways.retirementRule: Normal retirement rules plus accumulated investments. Homeowner status continues unless removed by an applicable Life Event.
pathways.educationMessage: Buying a home can create tax-relevant expenses, but the standard deduction may still be the better choice.
pathways.resultMessage: Homeownership gave you additional tax decisions, but owning a home did not automatically mean a bigger deduction.
pathways.developerNotes: Starting Homeowner status persists until removed by an applicable Life Event. Homeownership enables scenarios; it does not automatically force itemization.

pathways.name: Lifelong Learner
pathways.shortDescription: Education and career development remain recurring parts of your financial life.
pathways.startingCondition: Begin with normal income rules and Education Eligibility status active.
pathways.advantageRule: When an Education Opportunity occurs, receive the pathway's enhanced education treatment defined in Tax Rules.
pathways.challengeRule: Education spending does not automatically qualify for a tax benefit.
pathways.deductionRule: Education-related benefits are evaluated using current Tax Rules.
pathways.retirementRule: Normal retirement rules plus accumulated investments.
pathways.educationMessage: Education can interact with taxes in several ways, and eligibility rules determine whether a particular tax benefit applies.
pathways.resultMessage: Investing in education created additional tax decisions throughout your working life.
pathways.developerNotes: Do not hard-code an education credit or deduction amount here. Tax Rules should define the applicable benefit so annual law changes can be updated separately.

pathways.name: Side Hustler
pathways.shortDescription: You earn money from multiple sources, and those income sources can change throughout your career.
pathways.startingCondition: Draw two Income cards each regular-life round.
pathways.advantageRule: Draw two Income cards each regular-life round and use both income amounts. The cards may represent any combination of income types.
